title: Global Volunteer
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: an AIESEC programme where young people volunteer abroad on a project that contributes to one of the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while building leadership skills. Volunteers can choose the SDG that matters most to them.
Benefits named: living and working with people from many countries, meeting different viewpoints, taking on challenges outside the comfort zone.
How to apply (4 steps): 1) create an account on the AIESEC platform and complete the profile; 2) find a project with the search filters; 3) after applying, AIESEC makes contact and explains the selection process; 4) if selected, prepare logistics with AIESEC's help.
Support stated: AIESEC members in the home and host country help; help with the right visa; arrival pick-up information and departure instructions; clear expectations, cultural preparation and learning spaces before/during/after; an AIESEC representative accompanies the volunteer to the workplace on day one; job description, goals, working hours and duration are confirmed in advance.
Mandatory: life and health insurance. Volunteers receive information about accommodation and basic living costs.
Help contact: help@aiesec.net (general, not programme-specific).
Volatile site statistics (change over time, do not state them): opportunities in about 60 countries/territories, about 1,500 opportunities, thousands of volunteers per year.
NOT STATED on the page: eligibility (age, student status, nationality), whether membership is required, project duration and dates, deadlines, programme fees, cost of insurance/accommodation/living, stipend, flights, visa fees, language requirements, selection criteria, refund/cancellation rules, a programme-specific contact. No FAQ section.

title: Global Talent (professional internships)
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: AIESEC's international internships for young people, meant to build leadership skills and career prospects, across many fields. Benefits named: cross-cultural work experience, new skills, an edge through partner organisations. Matching is based on the candidate's background and profile. Premium-partner opportunities are described as open to top candidates across backgrounds.
Categories listed (approximate opportunity counts, volatile): Marketing, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Development, Business Administration, Finance, Other.
How to apply (4 steps): 1) create an account and complete the profile; 2) find an internship with the search filters; 3) after applying, AIESEC makes contact and explains the selection process; 4) if selected, prepare for travel with AIESEC's help.
Support stated: AIESEC members in home and host country; help with the right visa; arrival pick-up information and departure instructions; clear expectations, cultural preparation, learning spaces; AIESEC accompanies the intern to the workplace on day one and confirms job description, goals, working hours and duration.
Mandatory: life and health insurance. Interns receive information about accommodation and basic living costs (the page does not say whether these are provided or paid).
Help contact: help@aiesec.net.
Volatile site statistics (do not state): internships in about 67 countries/territories, 2,000+ internships worldwide.
NOT STATED on the page: eligibility (age, student/graduate status, nationality, minimum experience), internship length and dates, fees, whether internships are paid/unpaid or carry a stipend, what is included (flights, accommodation, meals), insurance cost, language requirements, deadlines, selection timeline, visa types by country, refund/cancellation, remote/part-time options. No FAQ section.

title: Global Teacher (teaching internships)
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: AIESEC's teaching internships abroad, meant to build leadership skills and career prospects. Interns gain experience in cross-cultural settings and add value to the school or institution. Opportunities range from first-time teaching to roles for experienced teachers.
Opportunities by region (approximate, volatile): Americas, Europe, Middle East and Africa, Asia Pacific; the page cites about 29 countries/territories.
How to apply (4 steps): 1) create an account and complete the profile; 2) find an internship with the search filters; 3) after applying, AIESEC makes contact and explains the selection process; 4) if selected, prepare travel and logistics with AIESEC's help.
Support stated: AIESEC members in home and host country before departure and while abroad; help with the right visa; arrival pick-up information and departure instructions; clear expectations, cultural preparation, learning spaces; a member accompanies the intern to the workplace on day one and confirms job description, goals, working hours and duration.
Mandatory: life and health insurance. Interns receive information about accommodation and basic living costs.
Help contact: help@aiesec.net.
NOT STATED on the page: eligibility (age, student/graduate status, nationality, qualifications, teaching experience, teaching licence), placement length and dates, fees, paid/unpaid or stipend, what is covered (flights, accommodation, visa), actual living-cost amounts, insurance cost, language of instruction or required proficiency, subjects/age groups/hours, deadlines, selection timeline, which 29 countries, refund/cancellation.

title: Become a member
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: joining AIESEC as a member of a local team, described as the world's largest youth-led organisation. Members learn through practical experience.
What members do: join a local team and a department. Five main areas listed: Customer Experience, Marketing, Sales & Business Development, Finance, Human Resources (names can vary between local teams). Selected members get an induction before starting a team role.
Benefits named: practical learning (self-management, interpersonal skills), a challenging environment for growing as a value-driven leader, a local and international network, chances to contribute through AIESEC programmes and further leadership roles, development of AIESEC's six values.
How to join (3 steps): 1) create an account on the AIESEC platform and complete the profile; 2) selection process: local teams recruit at specific times of the year, and after signing up you find out the next steps for your local team; 3) if successful, you join a team, get an induction and start a team role.
Volatile site statistics (do not state): over 35,000 active members, over 1,000,000 alumni, local teams in 100+ countries/territories.
The page also points people "looking for a different experience" to Global Talent, Global Teacher and Global Volunteer.
NOT STATED on the page: eligibility (age, nationality, education, language), any fee, time commitment, term length, whether members are paid, selection criteria and deadlines, recruitment dates of a specific local team, how to find/contact a local team, whether membership is required for exchange programmes, certificates or references.

title: About AIESEC
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What AIESEC is: a youth-run organisation ("by youth, for youth") whose stated cause is peace and fulfilment of humankind's potential; a global network that sees youth leadership as a responsibility.
Six values: Demonstrating Integrity, Striving for Excellence, Enjoying Participation, Acting Sustainably, Activating Leadership, Living Diversity.
History: founded in 1948 after the Second World War by young people from seven countries/territories to build cross-cultural understanding. 1977: present in 50 countries/territories on six continents. 2010: first year with more than 10,000 experiences delivered. 2015: youth leaders from 126 countries/territories met at UN headquarters about youth participation in the SDGs.
Status: non-governmental, not-for-profit; consultative status with the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC); affiliated with the UN Department of Public Information; member of ICMYO; recognised by UNESCO; AIESEC International is registered as a non-profit corporation in Montreal, Canada.
Offers for young people: Global Talent, Global Teacher, Global Volunteer, membership, Youth Speak, Youth for Global Goals. For organisations: hire an intern/teacher/volunteer, partner with AIESEC (16 global premium partners listed).
Contact/links: help@aiesec.net, blog.aiesec.org, alumni site aiesec-alumni.org, social channels (Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, YouTube).
Volatile site statistics (do not state): 100+ countries/territories, 5,000+ partner organisations, 30,000+ experiences per year.
FAQ answers on the page (paraphrased):
- Name: AIESEC (pronounced "eye-sek") was originally an acronym for Association Internationale des Étudiants en Sciences Économiques et Commerciales; it is no longer used as an acronym, just as the organisation's name. Members are called AIESECers.
- What it is: a global platform for young people to explore and develop their leadership potential; non-political, independent, not-for-profit; run by students and recent graduates of higher education. It does not discriminate on ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion or national/social origin. Alumni include business, NGO and world leaders, among them one Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
- Youth run: a network of young leaders under the age of 30 (this is the only age reference on the site and is not stated as a membership rule); all operations are managed by students and recent graduates; the global leadership teams are elected annually by the membership.
- Independent and non-partisan: not a subsidiary of, or dependent on, any other body; chooses peace above all and has no official political tendency.
- Origins: founded in 1948 in seven European countries/territories (the page names three founders; other sources name different founders, so do not state founders).
- Who can be an AIESECer: anyone who believes in AIESEC's vision, supports its mission and lives by its values, including partners and supportive parents. This describes belonging to the movement, not eligibility to become a member.
Site inconsistencies (do not state these figures): the site gives 100+, 109+ and 126 countries/territories in different places, and both "78 years" and "over 65 years".
NOT STATED on the page: anything specific to North Macedonia (local presence, committees, contacts, programmes, partners); how national and local entities are structured; leadership names, postal address, phone, budget.

title: YouthSpeak
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: an AIESEC initiative giving young people a platform to voice opinions and turn them into action.
Two parts: 1) a global survey, launched in 2016, collecting youth views on challenges, hopes and ambitions and bringing the collective voice to decision-makers, aiming to co-create the world young people want in 2030; 2) a forum (event) with short talks and skills workshops where participants learn about global and local issues, network and identify solutions, and learn how to contribute to the SDGs.
How to take part: take the survey; attend the forum.
Contact: help@aiesec.net (general).
NOT STATED on the page: age range/eligibility, whether AIESEC membership is needed, survey length/languages/deadline, who receives results, published reports, forum dates, locations, online or in-person format, cost, how to register.

title: Youth for Global Goals
source: aiesec.org, checked against raw page text in a browser (2026-11-12)
text:
What it is: an AIESEC initiative to raise awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) among young people and invite them to become leaders for the world. Direction to 2030: end extreme poverty, reduce inequalities, take climate action.
Activities: 1) spread awareness (learn about the SDGs); 2) understand how to contribute (YouthSpeak Forums); 3) take action, from small daily choices to a 6-week volunteering experience abroad on a cause the participant cares about; 4) find your goal (the SDGs explained through everyday examples; the "choose your goal" link leads to Global Volunteer).
Stated 2030 targets: 1,000,000+ people aware of the SDGs, 100,000+ understanding how to contribute, 50,000+ acting (the page does not say whether these are achieved or still targets). One awareness goal on the page is dated September 2017 and is outdated.
Contact: help@aiesec.net (general).
NOT STATED on the page: age limits, how to register, dates/locations of forums, costs, host countries or causes for volunteering, a dedicated contact.
